def factor_volume_momentum_temporal_decay(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    # get volume regime info
    is_high_vol, _, vol_ratio = alpha_tools.classify_volume_regime(df_copy["volume"], window=20)
    # compute returns
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    weighted_ret = ret * vol_ratio
    # 5-day and 20-day volume-weighted momentum
    sum_wt_ret_5 = weighted_ret.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
    sum_vol_5 = vol_ratio.rolling(5, min_periods=5).sum()
    factor_5 = sum_wt_ret_5 / sum_vol_5.replace(0, np.nan)
    sum_wt_ret_20 = weighted_ret.rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
    sum_vol_20 = vol_ratio.rolling(20, min_periods=20).sum()
    factor_20 = sum_wt_ret_20 / sum_vol_20.replace(0, np.nan)
    # adaptive momentum (same as parent)
    momentum = factor_5.where(is_high_vol > 0, factor_20)
    # days since last high vol day
    group = is_high_vol.cumsum()
    days_since = is_high_vol.groupby(group).cumcount()  # 0 on high vol day
    days_since = days_since.clip(upper=60)
    # temporal decay weight
    decay = 1.0 / (1.0 + days_since / 10.0)
    # apply decay
    signal = momentum * decay
    df_copy["factor_volume_momentum_temporal_decay"] = signal.fillna(0)
    return df_copy["factor_volume_momentum_temporal_decay"]

After a volume spike, the predictive power of momentum may fade as the market digests information; the signal is attenuated based on the elapsed time since the last spike. The core volume-weighted momentum uses a 5-day window during high volume regimes and a 20-day window otherwise, providing smooth adaptation. The decay factor is 1/(1+days_since/10), ensuring continuous attenuation without binary gating.
